title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks (abstract page)
note: Abstract page: v1 submitted 20 Aug 2026, v2 revised 6 Oct 2026. Two German district heating networks; hourly 24-hour forecasts, 12-week rolling context, ambient temperature. Headline: both zero-shot models beat all trained baselines on deterministic accuracy over the full-year benchmarks; CVRMSE on the main data set 12.48% (Chronos-2) and 13.07% (TabPFN-TS). Main benchmark assumes perfect weather.

title: Spoek et al., full text v2 (full-year results)
note: Full-year results: Chronos-2, TabPFN-TS and TFT are the top three in both networks by CVRMSE and by mean daily rank. After excluding 24 flagged Munich days (342 of 366 left): Chronos-2 11.83% [10.27, 13.76], TabPFN-TS 12.58%, TFT 14.24% [12.62, 16.20], Direct LGBM 15.47%, AutoGluon ensemble 16.09% (95% block-bootstrap intervals). The fetched text lost the CVRMSE column of the unfiltered table.

title: Spoek et al., full text v2 (weather-forecast sensitivity)
note: Weather sensitivity, Munich, 208 daily starts from 7 Jun to 31 Dec 2024: with ECMWF IFS HRES retrospective temperature (Open-Meteo single runs, previous 12:00 UTC run) instead of measured, CVRMSE goes from 11.41% to 12.56% for Chronos-2 (+10.1%) and from 11.89% to 12.77% for TabPFN-TS (+7.4%). Only the two zero-shot models were run; no trained baseline under forecast weather.

title: Search for an independent replication (third-party review page of v1)
note: One search for a replication of this study returned only the paper, its repository and aggregator pages; no independent replication. This review page of v1 (snippet only, not fetched) says the configuration was chosen on 2024 weeks that are also part of the evaluation year, and that TabPFN-TS was better calibrated than Chronos-2.

title: Spoek et al., full text v2 (design)
note: Design: Munich (private data) and Flensburg (public). Evaluation year 2024: a 24-hour forecast every 24 hours, 366 starts. Zero-shot models get a 12-week rolling context and realized future temperature; AutoGluon baselines are fitted once on 2023. Used tabpfn-time-series 1.1.0 and chronos-forecasting 2.2.2. No plan or registration mentioned.

title: Spoek et al., full text v2 (week-ahead appendix S4)
note: Appendix S4, week-ahead over the full year: 52 weekly forecasts of 168 hourly steps. Chronos-2 CVRMSE 15.64% [13.44, 18.05], MAE 109.7 kW; TabPFN-TS 17.06% [14.58, 19.94] (95% intervals). On three selected weeks TabPFN-TS had led; the full year reversed that. No trained baseline at this horizon. Units (kW) suggest Munich; the network is not named.

title: Spoek et al., full text v2 (baseline inputs, availability)
note: Temperature is a known covariate for the AutoGluon suite, but only the tabular models, DeepAR and TFT use its future values; naive, statistical, feed-forward and DLinear do not. Baselines see target history from the start of 2023, not the 12-week window. Code on GitHub and Zenodo; Munich data not public; Flensburg data public.

title: benspoek/tsfm-heatload (repository)
note: Authors' repository, MIT code, archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.23101871); cites the journal version in Energy and AI. Includes Flensburg data and scripts for the 2024 full-year runs of TabPFN-TS, Chronos-2 and AutoGluon (366 starts) and a Flensburg IFS weather-sensitivity run (208 starts, leads 11 to 34 h). Munich inputs excluded. Runs used a CUDA cluster.
